clue.text: One icily struck by player needing line-out courage

indicators.note: line-out tells us the line is taken out of the word for courage

parts.note: pluck is courage or nerve

explanation.surface: A rugby player at a line-out needs plenty of nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line-out' sounds like rugby, but it asks you to take L out of PLUCK. The definition describes the disc an ice hockey player strikes across the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice hockey player hits the small rubber disc across a frozen rink, so it is struck icily.

clue.text: Level weapon, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: par means level or equal
a lance is a long spear-like weapon

explanation.surface: A level weapon, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular way of speaking or idiom, as in 'legal jargon'.

clue.text: Stockholm and Santiago feature as such cities

definitions.text: Stockholm and Santiago feature as such cities

parts.words: Stockholm and Santiago feature as such cities
parts.note: Stockholm and Santiago are seats of national government, and each name also begins with an upper-case S

explanation.surface: Stockholm and Santiago appear in a list of a certain kind of city.
explanation.walkthrough: Both are national seats of government, and both 'feature' a big initial S, another sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Seats of national government are this kind of city, and the word also means upper-case letters.

clue.text: Tell police tribunal what one found at Wimbledon

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing on someone to the police
a court is a tribunal that hears cases

explanation.surface: An informer goes to the police and a tribunal, then turns up at a tennis tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: To GRASS is British slang for informing to the police; Wimbledon is the London tennis championship played on grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimbledon's tennis championships are played on lawn surfaces, so a turf playing area is what you would find there.

clue.text: Pedalled round, in skilful exhibition?

parts.note: rode means pedalled, as on a bicycle
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cyclist pedals in circles as a skilful display.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: an event showcasing cowboys' riding skills.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy show where riders display their skill with horses and cattle.

clue.text: Jungle beast is quiet before Asian ruler

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
ere is an old word for before
a khan is a ruler in Central Asia

explanation.surface: A jungle animal stays silent in front of an Asian potentate.
explanation.walkthrough: The tiger in Kipling's The Jungle Book.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger villain of Kipling's The Jungle Book is a famous wild animal of the forest.

clue.text: Commission some hot stuff that should prove acceptable

parts.note: a cut is a commission or share of the takings
the mustard is a hot condiment

explanation.surface: An agent's fee for some spicy produce should be satisfactory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commission' looks like a verb but is a noun: an agent's cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to meet the required standard, to be good enough.

clue.text: Like some children to come in due course?

definitions.text: Like some children to come in due course?

parts.words: Like some children to come in due course?
parts.note: reads as children who will arrive later, but due course hints at being due: babies not yet delivered

explanation.surface: Some children will turn up eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In due course' hints at a due date for a birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby not yet delivered is still to come, expected on its due date.

clue.text: Run to open up, man

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
overt means open, not hidden

explanation.surface: A man is told to run and open up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses R plus OVERT; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, typical of crossword clues where a man is any given name.

clue.text: Using pull, one may break a high-flyer's career

definitions.text: Using pull, one may break a high-flyer's career

parts.words: Using pull, one may break a high-flyer's career
parts.note: reads like influence wrecking a high achiever's prospects, but describes the cord a parachutist pulls to break a fall through the air

explanation.surface: Someone with influence brings down a rising star's career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' suggests influence and 'high-flyer' a successful person; really a skydiver tugs a cord to slow ('break') their careering descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A parachute is released by tugging a cord, which slows the falling jumper's headlong descent.

clue.text: Long ago, I started any number of stories

definitions.meaning: at some time in the distant past

definitions.text: I started any number of stories
definitions.meaning: the traditional opening phrase of fairy tales

explanation.surface: Long ago someone began telling countless tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale opening phrase means in the distant past.

clue.text: Each group of diners wanting food at least this

parts.note: a table is a party of people seated together for a meal

explanation.surface: Every party at a restaurant wants food that is at least palatable.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the end of the sentence: diners want their food to be at least fit to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The least diners ask of their food is that it is fit to consume, the meaning of the word.

clue.text: Hard right displacing left in piece for newspaper — Globe, perhaps

indicators.note: displacing means the new letters push out and take the place of the letter for left

parts.note: an article is a written piece for a newspaper
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
OK means right or correct

explanation.surface: A politically hard-right writer pushes out a leftist from a newspaper article, perhaps in the Globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard right' looks like politics, but is H plus OK, which replace L in ARTICLE. 'Globe' looks like a newspaper's name; it is a variety of vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe is a variety of that thistle-like vegetable, as opposed to the Jerusalem kind.

clue.text: Endlessly keep talking about Marx

indicators.note: Endlessly means the last letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: to harp on is to keep talking about something tediously

explanation.surface: Someone goes on and on about Karl Marx.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Karl Marx, but the definition is one of the Marx Brothers, the silent harpist.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Marx Brothers comedy team was known by this stage name and played the harp.

clue.text: Shady organisation dictating arrangements for the flat, say

definitions.text: Shady organisation dictating arrangements for the flat, say

parts.words: Shady organisation dictating arrangements for the flat, say
parts.note: reads like a dodgy gang controlling housing, but describes a planned set of shades deciding a home's decor

explanation.surface: A dubious outfit is controlling who lives in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shady organisation' suggests crooks; it really means an organised set of shades, which governs how a flat is decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned combination of hues and tints governs how a room or flat is decorated.

clue.text: Incompetent given high-level cover is an issue with Aussie soldiers

parts.note: a slouch is an incompetent or lazy person, as in 'no slouch'
a hat covers the top of the head

explanation.surface: An inept soldier is given a lofty position, causing trouble in the Australian army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means kit issued, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed hat with one side turned up is standard issue for Australian troops.

clue.text: One may be spoken of in different terms after one's executed

definitions.text: One may be spoken of in different terms after one's executed

parts.words: One may be spoken of in different terms after one's executed
parts.note: reads like the dead being remembered after execution, but describes a legal document that, once signed, means you are called by a new name

explanation.surface: Someone is talked about differently after being put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' suggests capital punishment; legally a document is executed when signed, changing the name you are known by.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal document used in Britain for changing one's name formally takes effect once signed.

clue.text: English in a diary's bad? Quite possibly

indicators.note: bad means these letters are put into a corrupted order

explanation.surface: Someone thinks the English in a diary is poor, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges E plus A DIARYS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'probably' or 'I suppose so', expressing likelihood.

clue.text: Get conceited, and get a little drunk

definitions.meaning: to become vain because of success or praise
to make someone tipsy, as strong drink does

explanation.surface: Someone becomes arrogant and slightly tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both success making someone vain and alcohol making them tipsy.

clue.text: Large groups of people cross eastern river

indicators.note: cross means the groups straddle the letter for eastern

parts.note: gangs are groups of people

explanation.surface: Big crowds wade across an eastern river.
explanation.definitionFit: The great sacred river of northern India is an example of a river.

clue.text: In distress ——— please frown!

definitions.meaning: grief or sorrow, deep emotional pain
an imperative to lour, scowl, made emphatic with do

explanation.surface: In deep sorrow, someone pleads for a scowl.
explanation.walkthrough: To lour is to frown; 'do lour!' is an emphatic plea.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief or sorrow is a literary word for great distress.

clue.text: Subtle quality one of Antony's audience finally missed

indicators.note: finally missed means the last letter of the phrase is lost

parts.note: Mark Antony's funeral speech in Julius Caesar is addressed to 'Friends, Romans, countrymen', so a member of his audience is a Roman

explanation.surface: A Roman in Antony's crowd failed to catch some subtle nuance at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtle quality' means a pervading air or flavour, as in a wine's bouquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle pervasive character, like an atmosphere or bouquet, is a figurative sense of fragrance.

clue.text: One hoping to be captain, who's already giving the orders?

definitions.meaning: in the navy this rank is just below captain
anyone in charge who issues orders

explanation.surface: An ambitious officer is already acting as if in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval rank sits just below captain, and the word also means anyone in command.

clue.text: Crews installing current for power supply

indicators.note: installing means the word for crews takes in the letter for current

parts.note: mans means crews, as in staffing a ship
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Teams are installing electric current for the electricity supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crews' is a verb: to man.
explanation.definitionFit: The main supply of electricity or water to a building.

clue.text: Course of sticky food is reasonable

parts.note: goo is a sticky substance, here food
a dish is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A course of gooey food turns out to be acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairly good or acceptable, as the suffix -ish softens the adjective.

clue.text: Having returned to pavilion, not out?

definitions.text: Having returned to pavilion, not out?

parts.words: Having returned to pavilion, not out?
parts.note: reads as cricket, a batsman back in the pavilion who was not dismissed, but simply describes being inside a building rather than outside

explanation.surface: A cricketer has walked back to the pavilion without being dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the pavilion is the clubhouse and 'not out' an undefeated batsman; here both just mean being inside rather than outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Being back inside a building and not outside means being within its walls.

clue.text: Recent sets used afresh for audition

indicators.note: used afresh means these letters are put to new use in a fresh order

explanation.surface: New film sets are reused for an actor's tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used afresh' rearranges RECENT SETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A film audition where an actor is filmed to judge suitability for a role.

clue.text: Murder a tinker outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for a tinker goes around the letter A

parts.note: a tinker, a mischievous rascal, is sly or roguish

explanation.surface: A travelling tinker is killed out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tinker' looks like the travelling mender of pots; here it is a rascal, so SLY, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill violently is a literary synonym for murdering someone.
